title: KV stripe & batch-aware allocator harmonization for long-context LLMs
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Reduce peak GPU fragmentation and tail latency for long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants by introducing a KV-cache striping layout and batch-aware allocator heuristics that harmonize working set placement with continuous batching behavior. Scope includes PoC allocator changes, microbenchmarks across model variants, integration with existing KV eviction windows, and rollout gating in runtime-1.22.
acceptance_criteria: Peak GPU memory fragmentation reduced by >= 12% across target models under representative long-context workloads (seq_len >= 32k).
99th percentile generation latency does not increase by more than 5% for P50 batching SLOs; throughput improves or remains flat under continuous batching.
Automated integration test added to CI that validates KV stripe placement invariants and eviction correctness for sharded KV setups.
Rollout plan and rollback strategy documented in Confluence and linked PRs; runtime-1.22 release notes include the change and opt-out flag.
technical_notes: Approach: split KV residency into 3 'stripes' by key-range and prefer hot-slab placements for stripe 0 to reduce cross-slab hops during attention retrieval.

Batch-aware allocator: allocator tracks recent batch sequence-length histogram and biases placements to co-locate likely-reused KV slices within the same GPU slab to reduce cross-slab copies during continuous batching.
Eviction harmony: extend existing eviction window heuristic to consider stripe affinity and per-variant working set decay rates (shorter decay for Qwen-large longctx variants observed empirically).
Memory overhead: PoC adds ~1.5% metadata overhead for stripe maps; target is <2.5% in release build.
Compatibility: changes are gated behind feature flag runtime.kv_stripe_alloc.enabled and a per-model profile toggle to avoid regressions for constrained memory models.
progress_updates: 2026-02-21: Spike completed — microbench harness measuring slab locality and KV lookup latencies across Llama-70b, Mistral-22b, Qwen-1.5-longctx. Observed 14-18% reduction in cross-slab KV misses in synthetic steady-state workloads.

2026-02-26: Implemented PoC stripe map and a minimal allocator hook in the runtime branch feature/kv-stripe. Benchmarks show 8% improvement in tokens/sec for continuous batching at seq_len=24k for Qwen variant.

2026-03-03: Discovered a rare race during concurrent eviction+placement under bursty ingress. Mitigation: introduce per-stripe eviction locks with cooperative backoff. Added unit tests that reproduce race locally.
2026-03-08: Internal review with Performance team — agreed to add adaptive stripe sizing (ratio per model variant) to avoid cold-start penalties for small footprints. Added as next subtask.
2026-03-10: End-to-end integration tests passing in staging with runtime-1.22 build; opened PR #9123 and flagged for PM/Release review.
review_comments: PM (Riley Gomez): please quantify rollback cost and ensure customers on Dedicated can opt-out via config before GA.
Design (Nadia Ortiz): allocate a small UX hint in Console to show when stripe allocation is active and the model-level profile in use.
Security (Samir Kaur): confirm stripe metadata does not expose key material and follows KMS encryption-at-rest policies. We will run a brief threat model for metadata scoping.
Infra (Diego Morales): watch out for scheduler interactions when feature flag toggles at runtime; prefer restart-on-toggle for first iteration.
qa_notes: Create long-tail perf matrix: run combinations of batch sizes {1,4,8,16}, seq_lens {8k,16k,24k,32k}, model variants {llama-70b, mistral-22b, qwen-1.5-longctx}.
Add fault-injection test: force stripe lock contention and validate graceful degradation (fallback to legacy allocator).
Verify metric instrumention: KV hit/miss by stripe, slab crossing counts, eviction rates, and per-token latency breakdowns in Grafana dashboard panel.
Run Dedicated capacity smoke test to ensure no regression in autoscaler behavior for pre-pinned GPU pools.
